- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or volatile (alternating ±0.33), model often underestimates or lags; adjust upward to capture mean reversion or momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overcorrects or fails to sustain momentum; cap forecast rise to 3–4% below peak or align with sentiment decay.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply a 1–2 day lag correction downward.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate mean price in early window; apply a 0.5–1.0% downward bias for first 7–10 days if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- If sentiment history shows repeated +0.33/-0.33 alternation, model often misreads trend; treat as “no clear direction” and forecast around 1–2% below recent 7-day average.
